verdict.rationale: Next.js documents several features aimed at large codebases: Multi-Zones micro-frontends for splitting apps across teams, codemods for upgrades, a bundle analyzer, and server components that add no client-side JavaScript. Community reports are mixed. One user calls the App Router great after three production-scale projects, while another says their large Next.js app was 'weird, slow, cumbersome' and that behaviors are poorly documented. missing for 10: first-party guidance on scaling maintainability as teams grow, consistent independent corroboration that large apps stay fast and maintainable, evidence on build/dev performance at scale.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build large applications that stay fast and maintainable as my team and codebase grow

citations.quote: Learn how to build micro-frontends using Next.js Multi-Zones to deploy multiple Next.js apps under a single domain.
Use codemods to upgrade your Next.js codebase when new features are released.
Learn how to analyze and optimize your application's server and client bundles with the Next.js Bundle Analyzer for Turbopack
Add components without sending additional client-side JavaScript.
